title: Probabilistic hysteresis matrix and backstop fallback orchestration
creator: Liam O'Neil
description: Implement a probabilistic hysteresis-based circuit system that produces smooth, staged fallbacks across dependency/model/tenant dimensions. The goal is to avoid hard all-or-nothing opens and instead use a scored approach that transitions traffic fractions to safe fallback actions based on sustained degradation signals. Core requirements: define score inputs, mapping function to open probability, hysteresis windows and cooldown, fallback hierarchy, tenant fairness, and multi-region reroute policies. The implementation must preserve tenant semantics (auth, data isolation, idempotency) and provide comprehensive telemetry for alerting and postmortems.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Initial triage: scoped as a systems-level implementation that replaces ad-hoc breakers with a probabilistic hysteresis matrix. Assigned to Aisha. Action: prototype threshold functions and create test harness.

2026-02-25 - Design review: decided on three axis inputs to the hysteresis scoring: error rate (5xx), p99 latency delta, and GPU queue depth. Each axis weighted per dependency criticality; discussed per-tenant SLO tiers (gold/silver/bronze) affecting sensitivity.
2026-02-27 - PM feedback (Marina Chen): emphasise tenant isolation and safe rollbacks; add explicit procedure for KV-cache rehydration after fallback to avoid cold-start latency spikes.

2026-03-01 - Engineering note: implemented a proof-of-concept in sandbox using weighted rolling-window scoring and a Bernoulli tripper that flips open with probability p(score). Observed smoother partial degradations under spike tests.

2026-03-03 - Staging test results: regional failover drill passed for synthetic latency spike to model-v1; saw transient tail increases when backstop switched to quantized model; added 30s hysteresis window and exponential cooldown to avoid flip-flop.

2026-03-05 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428 - adds hysteresis-matrix config, probabilistic-tripper module, and orchestration hooks for fallback actions. Requesting security review and staging rollout.

2026-03-06 - Next steps: finalize telemetry (per-tenant SLO buckets + synthetic probes), add chaos test for partial region network partitions, coordinate with Console team for rollout UI knobs and kill-switches.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New hysteresis matrix calculates a trip score for each (dependency, model, tenant) and exposes score and state metrics.
2) Probabilistic tripper opens circuits progressively (partial traffic fraction) instead of all-or-nothing at first detection.
3) Backstop fallback orchestration supports: local degrade to quantized variant, regional reroute, cached-response, and error-typed short-circuit with consistent tenant semantics.
4) Multi-region failover: when a region's aggregate trip score exceeds threshold for configured window, traffic is rerouted according to policy with staged percentages and automatic rollback on recovery.
5) Observability: dashboards for score components, per-tenant SLO buckets, synthetic probe failures, and alerting rules mapped to severity and paging.
6) Chaos and load tests added; no customer-impacting error spikes during staged rollout beyond defined SLO windows.
implementation_notes:
- Hysteresis matrix: discrete time sliding windows per metric with exponential decay. Score = w1*err_rate_norm + w2*latency_delta_norm + w3*gpu_queue_norm. Normalize using 95th percentile baselines per dependency.
- Probabilistic tripper: map score->p(open) using logistic curve; when circuit 'partially open' assign fraction f of requests to fallback using weighted random sampling to preserve fairness.
- Backstops: hierarchy = in-region quantized model -> regional replica -> cached response -> short-circuit error with user-facing guidance. Maintain idempotency and request affinity when rerouting stateful calls.
- Cooldown and re-introduction: use exponential backoff plus controlled canary percentages (5%, 20%, 50%, 100) with success thresholds per step.
- Tenant safety: enforce per-tenant max-fallthrough-rate and allocate tokens for golden tenants to avoid complete shed. Implement fair queuing by token buckets keyed by tenant id.
- Config: YAML-driven profiles for dependency criticality and SLO tiers; runtime overrides via Console with audit logs.
- Telemetry: emit score components, open-state fraction, fallback action counts, rehydrate latencies, and per-tenant dropped requests. Correlate with traces for debug.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for normalization and logistic mapping edge cases.
- Integration tests in sandbox simulating: sustained error-rate spike, tail-latency spike, GPU saturation, and combined failures.
- Chaos experiments: region-level network egress degradation, delayed RPCs, and partial data-plane outages.
- Performance tests: measure additional latency introduced by probabilistic routing under 95% P99 load.
- Staged rollout: dark launch metrics for 48h, canary to 5% for 1h, expand to 25% for 4h with automated rollback on alert, then progressive ramp.
- Post-rollout validation: verify no SLO regressions for top-50 tenants and validate KV-cache warmup reduces cold-starts below threshold.
rollout_steps:
1) Dark launch: enable scoring and telemetry only (no routing). 48h observation.
2) Canary: enable probabilistic routing for non-critical tenants in staging region (5%). 1h observation.
3) Expand canary: 25% for 4h, monitor alerts and top-100 tenant metrics.
4) Regional pilot: enable full routing in a secondary region for 10 production tenants.
5) Global: staged region-by-region ramp with rollback windows; Console feature flag and kill-switch available at each step.
risk_and_mitigation:
- Risk: rapid flip-flop causing request thrash. Mitigation: minimum hysteresis window + exponential cooldown and require sustained score above threshold for multiple windows.
- Risk: tenants experience degradations due to cold cache after fallback. Mitigation: prioritized cache rehydration and pre-warming heuristics; increase cache retention for impacted tenants during rollout.
- Risk: incorrect per-tenant weight config causing unfair shedding. Mitigation: run fairness simulation tool and provide 'golden tenant' safelists.
- Risk: operational complexity in Console. Mitigation: CLI-first rollout and minimal UI surface for initial release; document runbooks and train on-call.
